entities.name: N-Acetyl to N-Ethyl Reduction
observations: The encoded transformation is CC(=O)NCC1(O)CCN(C)CC1 to CCNCC1(O)CCN(C)CC1, converting an N-acetyl group into an N-ethyl group.
This is reductive deoxygenation of an amide, not ordinary hydrolysis or hydrazinolysis.
The exact indexed ORD record is the reverse acetylation and does not document reduction conditions.

entities.name: Borane
observations: A closely relevant record supports borane-mediated reduction or cleavage of an N-acyl substrate to an amine; the listed medium includes a THF-type cyclic ether, followed by HCl/NaOH workup.
The retrieved record does not provide a reliable temperature or yield.

entities.name: Borane THF reduction workup
observations: Plausible conditions are BH3, commonly as BH3·THF, followed by acidic and basic aqueous workup; these are evidence-supported at the reagent-class level, not as a fully specified exact protocol.
LiOH aqueous or glycol conditions appeared only in non-matching fuzzy records and should not be treated as evidence for this substrate.
